inct empty state. Following is explicit, cycle-checked, and saved per character across reloads. Only the follow target is saved; fresh validated party data is required before resuming. Temporary peer expiry or unavailable focus preserves the follow intent while waiting. Missing quests preserve the saved follow target and current navigation, with a Waiting for a shared quest status in PQL. No missing-quest modal interrupts play. Periodic ownership checks resume following when the current focused quest enters the local quest log, and a new shared focus also resumes immediately; neither requires selecting Follow again. Cleared focus preserves the follow and personal navigation. Party departure, disband, raid conversion, ignore, and addon disable clear the saved intent. PQL uses ordinary Blizzard mini quest POI atlases in each owned quest/player cell; local buttons focus a quest and teammates’ active quest buttons start following. Inactive teammate buttons are read-only and gray. All buttons retain full opacity. While following, every button is gray except the followed member’s active quest; choosing your own focus or another member’s active quest asks for confirmation before ending or switching the follow. Without a follow, your buttons and teammates’ active quests retain their colors. Header menus retain focus details and following controls. Cancel leaves the follow intact, and a follow-identity token rejects confirmations from a superseded follow. Use `/qt preview unfollow` or the isolated compare preview to exercise the warning. While actively syncing a valid shared quest, native quest-tracker changes restore the last followed focus and ask before applying the new quest or clearing focus; Cancel keeps following. While waiting, or after the previous quest leaves the local log, native selections caused by quest pickup or turn-in establish a new local baseline without ending the follow. Restoration uses guarded public APIs after the tracking event, without modifying Blizzard callbacks, so the native selection may briefly change before restoration. Explicit waypoint navigation through QT stops following directly. A failed restoration stops following without repeated writes; a failed confirmed quest setter preserves the follow. QT setter echoes do not prompt. Restricted changes retain the latest received intent, then recheck current membership, ownership, and follow state before applying. Failed setters are reported without repeated retries.
